Series::LinearAlgAccessor::norm¶

Back to Series::LinearAlgAccessor API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::LinearAlgAccessor::norm() const
Series SeriesLinearAlgProxy::norm() const

What It Does¶

norm() measures the Euclidean length of the entire Series. It squares every element, adds those squares, and takes one square root:

||x||2 = sqrt(sum_i x_i^2)

For a matrix this same calculation is called the Frobenius norm. Dimensions do not identify independent rows, columns, or batches here: all elements participate in one global reduction and the result is a rank-zero scalar.

Length In Any Number Of Dimensions¶

The norm answers “how large is this value as one point?” A vector [3,4] has length 5; reshaping the same values does not change that length. This makes the method useful for residual size, parameter magnitude, and normalization, but not for obtaining one norm per row or per batch item.

Returns¶

Series A scalar Series with shape=[].

Gradient¶

Away from zero, each element receives x_i / ||x||2. An element contributes more sensitivity in proportion to its share of the total length. At the zero input the implementation returns a zero subgradient rather than dividing by zero.

Examples¶

Example 1. The familiar 3-4-5 triangle becomes a scalar length.

auto vector = pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0});
std::cout << vector.linearalg.norm() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=5

Example 2. A matrix is reduced globally, not row by row.

auto matrix = pluss::make_series({{1.0, 2.0}, {2.0, 1.0}});
std::cout << matrix.linearalg.norm() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=3.1622777

Example 3. Reverse mode points in the input’s direction.

auto vector = pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0});
vector.tracks_slope_(true);
vector.linearalg.norm().reverse();
std::cout << vector.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0.6, 0.8]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • norm() is global; it has no dimension or keepdim parameter.

  • The result is a scalar Series, not a C++ double.

  • Squaring very large values can overflow and very small values can underflow.

Summary¶

norm() returns one Euclidean/Frobenius magnitude for the complete input.

See Also¶

  • Series::div: divide by a computed norm to rescale values.

  • Series::LinearAlgAccessor::dot: inner product of two vectors.
